$comment: Cross-language webhook HMAC conformance vector for issue #2455.
PROVENANCE: every field below was PRINTED BY THE RUST SIGNER, not
hand-written and not computed by either SDK. It was produced by
temporarily adding a #[test] to the `mod tests` in src/subscriptions.rs
that calls the production helpers verbatim:
let key_hex = sha256_hex(secret);
let canonical = format!("{ts}.{body}");
let sig = hmac_sha256_hex(&key_hex, &canonical);
and running `cargo test --lib <name> -- --nocapture`. Those are the exact
two calls the dispatch path makes at src/subscriptions.rs:983-990. The
temporary test was reverted; src/ is untouched by this change.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: sdk/python/tests/test_client.py previously computed
its own 'expected' signature with the SAME wrong construction the
implementation used, then asserted the implementation agreed with itself.
It passed while the SDK could not verify a single real delivery. A fixture
the SDK cannot influence is the only thing that makes the test load-bearing.
TO REGENERATE (only if the daemon's signing contract intentionally changes):
re-add such a test, run it, paste the printed values here, and update BOTH
SDK suites. Do NOT edit these values to make a failing test pass — a
mismatch means the SDK drifted from the daemon.
CONTRACT: signature = HMAC-SHA256(key = SHA256(secret), "{timestamp}.{body}")
emitted as `sha256=<hex>` in X-AI-Memory-Signature, with the timestamp in
the separate X-AI-Memory-Timestamp header.
